<subject>Re: Results of the Bankruptcy Hearing for Triton Capital's Issues With Corporate Lending</subject>
<body>
You should have the email below in your inbox talking about the counterparties on our syndicated facility. Contact Triton Capital regarding the email below once you find out if we are able to proceed without maintaining a reserve requirement.
</body>
<quoted>
-----Original Message-----
From: Owen, Julia
Sent: Tuesday, April 29, 2025 4:09 PM
To: Hamilton, Derek; Hutchinson, Ross; Johnston, Laura; Marian Hussain, Debra
Cc: Sophie Jr., Ed; Mann, Gregory; m796@maroragroup.com'; s692@soldynlabs.com'; Barker, Mathew; Amy, Joshua; Garza, Kathleen; m789@trinorco.com'; j244@trinorco.com'; Holmes, Sean A.
Subject: Results of the Bankruptcy Hearing for Triton Capital's Issues With Corporate Lending

Here is a quick update on how Triton Capital's bankruptcy hearing went last week for the Corporate Lending issues:

Triton Capital agreed to withdraw the portion of their motion that was associated with Corporate Lending. The lender admitted that Corporate Lending has been drawing on their credit facilities and have been servicing payments since the bankruptcy petition date.
The £1.8 million claim that Triton Capital had been including in Halcyon's "set off amount" (i.e. the remaining facility fees for Corporate Lending's agreements until the end of the contract terms) was pulled from Triton Capital's Motion.
The minimum liquidity reserve monthly requirement should no longer be imposed by the lender (Note: Originally Triton Capital appeared to be using Corporate Lending's minimum reserve to offset Treasury & Credit Risk obligations).

I would recommend that you challenge Triton Capital's operations team, if they continue to say that Corporate Lending must be maintaining a minimum reserve in your facility. If you have any problems, please let me know and I will get our outside counsel involved again.

Thanks,
Julia Owen
</quoted>
